claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been reported in obesity and insulin resistance.
source: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been reported in obesity and insulin resistance, but primary genetic mitochondrial dysfunction is generally not associated with these, arguing against a straightforward causal relationship.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field, supported by established scientific knowledge and likely citations in the broader literature.

claim: Primary genetic mitochondrial dysfunction is generally not associated with obesity and insulin resistance.
source: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been reported in obesity and insulin resistance, but primary genetic mitochondrial dysfunction is generally not associated with these, arguing against a straightforward causal relationship.
evidence: This statement draws on established scientific consensus about mitochondrial disorders.

claim: The p.Arg707Trp mutation in MFN2 causes a syndrome of lower body adipose loss, leptin-deficient severe upper body adipose overgrowth, and insulin resistance in humans.
source: A rare exception, recently identified in humans, is a syndrome of lower body adipose loss, leptin-deficient severe upper body adipose overgrowth, and insulin resistance caused by the p.Arg707Trp mutation in MFN2, encoding mitofusin 2.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior research findings, as indicated by the context of the manuscript.

claim: Mfn2R707W/R707W knock-in mice were generated and phenotyped on chow and high fat diets.
source: To address this, Mfn2R707W/R707W knock-in mice were generated and phenotyped on chow and high fat diets.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: Electron microscopy revealed adipose-specific mitochondrial morphological abnormalities in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Electron microscopy revealed adipose-specific mitochondrial morphological abnormalities.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from electron microscopy presented in the manuscript.

claim: Oxidative phosphorylation measured in isolated mitochondria was unperturbed in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Oxidative phosphorylation measured in isolated mitochondria was unperturbed, but the cellular integrated stress response was activated in adipose tissue.
evidence: This is based on direct experimental measurements reported in the study.

claim: The cellular integrated stress response was activated in adipose tissue of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Oxidative phosphorylation measured in isolated mitochondria was unperturbed, but the cellular integrated stress response was activated in adipose tissue.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing ISR markers in adipose tissue.

claim: Fat mass and distribution were unchanged in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Fat mass and distribution, body weight, and systemic glucose and lipid metabolism were unchanged, however serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations, and their secretion from adipose explants were reduced.
evidence: This is based on body composition measurements and tissue weight data presented in the study.

claim: Body weight was unchanged in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Fat mass and distribution, body weight, and systemic glucose and lipid metabolism were unchanged, however serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations, and their secretion from adipose explants were reduced.
evidence: This is supported by longitudinal body weight measurements.

claim: Systemic glucose and lipid metabolism were unchanged in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Fat mass and distribution, body weight, and systemic glucose and lipid metabolism were unchanged, however serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations, and their secretion from adipose explants were reduced.
evidence: This is based on serum biochemistry and glucose/insulin tolerance tests.

claim: Serum leptin concentrations were reduced in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Fat mass and distribution, body weight, and systemic glucose and lipid metabolism were unchanged, however serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations, and their secretion from adipose explants were reduced.
evidence: This is supported by serum leptin measurements at multiple timepoints.

claim: Serum adiponectin concentrations were reduced in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Fat mass and distribution, body weight, and systemic glucose and lipid metabolism were unchanged, however serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations, and their secretion from adipose explants were reduced.
evidence: This is supported by serum adiponectin measurements.

claim: Leptin secretion from adipose explants was reduced in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Fat mass and distribution, body weight, and systemic glucose and lipid metabolism were unchanged, however serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations, and their secretion from adipose explants were reduced.
evidence: This is based on ex vivo adipose explant secretion experiments.

claim: Adiponectin secretion from adipose explants was reduced in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Fat mass and distribution, body weight, and systemic glucose and lipid metabolism were unchanged, however serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations, and their secretion from adipose explants were reduced.
evidence: This is based on ex vivo adipose explant secretion experiments.

claim: Pharmacological induction of the integrated stress response in wild-type adipocytes reduced secretion of leptin and adiponectin.
source: Pharmacological induction of the integrated stress response in wild-type adipocytes also reduced secretion of leptin and adiponectin, suggesting an explanation for the in vivo findings.
evidence: This is based on experiments treating primary adipocytes with thapsigargin and tunicamycin.

claim: The p.Arg707Trp MFN2 mutation selectively perturbs mitochondrial morphology in adipose tissue.
source: These data suggest that the p.Arg707Trp MFN2 mutation selectively perturbs mitochondrial morphology and activates the integrated stress response in adipose tissue.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the electron microscopy and molecular data presented.

claim: The p.Arg707Trp MFN2 mutation activates the integrated stress response in adipose tissue.
source: These data suggest that the p.Arg707Trp MFN2 mutation selectively perturbs mitochondrial morphology and activates the integrated stress response in adipose tissue.
evidence: This is based on qPCR, western blot, and transcriptomic data showing ISR activation.

claim: In mice, the p.Arg707Trp MFN2 mutation does not disrupt most adipocyte functions or systemic metabolism.
source: In mice, this does not disrupt most adipocyte functions or systemic metabolism, whereas in humans it is associated with pathological adipose remodelling and metabolic disease.
evidence: This is based on the normal body composition and metabolic parameters observed in the mice.

claim: In humans, the p.Arg707Trp MFN2 mutation is associated with pathological adipose remodelling and metabolic disease.
source: In mice, this does not disrupt most adipocyte functions or systemic metabolism, whereas in humans it is associated with pathological adipose remodelling and metabolic disease.
evidence: This is based on prior clinical observations cited in the manuscript.

claim: Disproportionate effects on leptin secretion may relate to cell autonomous induction of the integrated stress response in both mice and humans.
source: In both species, disproportionate effects on leptin secretion may relate to cell autonomous induction of the integrated stress response.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Most patients with inherited mitochondrial disorders have a neurological phenotype.
source: Instead, most patients with inherited mitochondrial disorders have a neurological phenotype, although multisystem involvement is common (Gorman et al., 2016; Suomalainen and Battersby, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on mitochondrial disorders.

claim: Multisystem involvement is common in inherited mitochondrial disorders.
source: Instead, most patients with inherited mitochondrial disorders have a neurological phenotype, although multisystem involvement is common (Gorman et al., 2016; Suomalainen and Battersby, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Biallelic R707W mutations in MFN2 were identified in patients with extreme upper body adiposity and lower body lipodystrophy.
source: We (Rocha et al., 2017) and others (Sawyer et al., 2015; Capel et al., 2018; Carr et al., 2015; Masingue et al., 2017; Piscosquito et al., 2015) recently identified biallelic R707W mutations in the nuclear MFN2 gene in patients with a remarkable adipose phenotype characterised by extreme upper body adiposity (lipomatosis) and lower body lipodystrophy.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior clinical studies.

claim: Affected patients with MFN2 R707W mutations showed non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, dyslipidaemia and insulin resistant type 2 diabetes.
source: Affected patients also showed non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, dyslipidaemia and insulin resistant type 2 diabetes, likely secondary to the changes in adipose tissue.
evidence: This is based on clinical observations from prior studies.

claim: The metabolic abnormalities in MFN2 R707W patients are likely secondary to changes in adipose tissue.
source: Affected patients also showed non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, dyslipidaemia and insulin resistant type 2 diabetes, likely secondary to the changes in adipose tissue.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pattern of clinical findings.

claim: MFN2 encodes mitofusin 2, a mitochondrial outer membrane protein that plays a key role in mitochondrial fusion and tethering to other organelles.
source: MFN2 encodes mitofusin 2, a mitochondrial outer membrane protein that plays a key role in mitochiondrial fusion and tethering to other organelles (Giacomello et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about MFN2 function, supported by a citation.

claim: Patients with heterozygous complete loss-of-function mutations in MFN2 exhibit axonal peripheral neuropathy known as Charcot-Marie Tooth type 2 A (CMT2A).
source: Like patients with heterozygous complete loss-of-function mutations in MFN2, patients with the R707W mutation also often exhibit axonal peripheral neuropathy known as Charcot-Marie Tooth type 2 A (CMT2A) (Chung et al., 2006; Verhoeven et al., 2006; Neusch et al., 2007), but the adipose and metabolic phenotype has uniquely been associated with the R707W allele to date.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior clinical studies.

claim: Patients with the MFN2 R707W mutation often exhibit axonal peripheral neuropathy (CMT2A).
source: Like patients with heterozygous complete loss-of-function mutations in MFN2, patients with the R707W mutation also often exhibit axonal peripheral neuropathy known as Charcot-Marie Tooth type 2 A (CMT2A) (Chung et al., 2006; Verhoeven et al., 2006; Neusch et al., 2007), but the adipose and metabolic phenotype has uniquely been associated with the R707W allele to date.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior clinical studies.

claim: The adipose and metabolic phenotype has uniquely been associated with the MFN2 R707W allele.
source: Like patients with heterozygous complete loss-of-function mutations in MFN2, patients with the R707W mutation also often exhibit axonal peripheral neuropathy known as Charcot-Marie Tooth type 2 A (CMT2A) (Chung et al., 2006; Verhoeven et al., 2006; Neusch et al., 2007), but the adipose and metabolic phenotype has uniquely been associated with the R707W allele to date.
evidence: This is based on the absence of reports of this phenotype with other MFN2 mutations.

claim: Elevated serum lactate was observed in patients with the MFN2 R707W mutation.
source: Evidence suggesting that the MFN2 R707W mutation does disrupt mitochondrial function in humans includes elevated serum lactate in affected patients, abnormal mitochondrial morphology seen on transmission electron microscopy of affected adipose tissue (Rocha et al., 2017), and strong transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial dysfunction and activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in the same tissue.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior clinical observations.

claim: Abnormal mitochondrial morphology was seen on transmission electron microscopy of affected adipose tissue in MFN2 R707W patients.
source: Evidence suggesting that the MFN2 R707W mutation does disrupt mitochondrial function in humans includes elevated serum lactate in affected patients, abnormal mitochondrial morphology seen on transmission electron microscopy of affected adipose tissue (Rocha et al., 2017), and strong transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial dysfunction and activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in the same tissue.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Strong transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial dysfunction and activation of the integrated stress response were observed in adipose tissue of MFN2 R707W patients.
source: Evidence suggesting that the MFN2 R707W mutation does disrupt mitochondrial function in humans includes elevated serum lactate in affected patients, abnormal mitochondrial morphology seen on transmission electron microscopy of affected adipose tissue (Rocha et al., 2017), and strong transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial dysfunction and activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in the same tissue.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Plasma leptin concentrations were very low in MFN2 R707W patients despite normal or raised whole body adipose mass.
source: Despite normal or raised whole body adipose mass, and the relatively normal histological appearance of lipomatous upper body fat, plasma leptin concentrations were very low in the patients reported by Rocha et al (Rocha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior clinical observations.

claim: One patient reported by Sawyer et al. had undetectable serum leptin (<0.6 ng/mL).
source: This observation was supported by Sawyer et al. who reported one patient with undetectable serum leptin (<0.6 ng/mL) (Sawyer et al., 2015) and Capel et al. who described five patients with serum leptin concentrations <1.6 ng/mL despite body mass indices (BMIs) within the normal range (Capel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior clinical report.

claim: Five patients described by Capel et al. had serum leptin concentrations <1.6 ng/mL despite BMIs within the normal range.
source: This observation was supported by Sawyer et al. who reported one patient with undetectable serum leptin (<0.6 ng/mL) (Sawyer et al., 2015) and Capel et al. who described five patients with serum leptin concentrations <1.6 ng/mL despite body mass indices (BMIs) within the normal range (Capel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior clinical report.

claim: Circulating leptin concentration correlates with fat mass.
source: Circulating leptin concentration correlates with fat mass, and is usually higher in women than men, with some adipose depots reported to release more than others (Montague et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Circulating leptin is usually higher in women than men.
source: Circulating leptin concentration correlates with fat mass, and is usually higher in women than men, with some adipose depots reported to release more than others (Montague et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Some adipose depots release more leptin than others.
source: Circulating leptin concentration correlates with fat mass, and is usually higher in women than men, with some adipose depots reported to release more than others (Montague et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Leptin secretion is increased by insulin stimulation.
source: Leptin secretion is increased by insulin stimulation (Cammisotto et al., 2005) but this effect is modest in the context of serum leptin concentrations.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The effect of insulin on leptin secretion is modest in the context of serum leptin concentrations.
source: Leptin secretion is increased by insulin stimulation (Cammisotto et al., 2005) but this effect is modest in the context of serum leptin concentrations.
evidence: This is an interpretation of prior research findings.

claim: Adipose depots that secrete higher leptin have increased LEP mRNA.
source: Adipose depots that secrete higher leptin have increased LEP mRNA and, at least in vitro, LEP mRNA increases in response to insulin stimulation (Alvarez-Guaita et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: LEP mRNA increases in response to insulin stimulation in vitro.
source: Adipose depots that secrete higher leptin have increased LEP mRNA and, at least in vitro, LEP mRNA increases in response to insulin stimulation (Alvarez-Guaita et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Most neuropathy-associated MFN2 mutations are located within the protein's GTPase domain.
source: Most neuropathy-associated MFN2 mutations are located within the protein's GTPase domain (Kijima et al., 2005; Züchner et al., 2004; Feely et al., 2011; Stuppia et al., 2015), but to date, all patients with MFN2-associated multiple symmetric lipomatosis (MSL) have had at least one R707W allele.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior genetic studies.

claim: All patients with MFN2-associated multiple symmetric lipomatosis have had at least one R707W allele.
source: Most neuropathy-associated MFN2 mutations are located within the protein's GTPase domain (Kijima et al., 2005; Züchner et al., 2004; Feely et al., 2011; Stuppia et al., 2015), but to date, all patients with MFN2-associated multiple symmetric lipomatosis (MSL) have had at least one R707W allele.
evidence: This is based on review of prior clinical reports.

claim: Most cases of MFN2-associated lipomatosis have been homozygous for the R707W mutation.
source: Most cases have been homozygous for the R707W mutation, with others compound heterozygous for R707W and a second, functionally null mutation (Rocha et al., 2017; Sawyer et al., 2015; Capel et al., 2018; Carr et al., 2015; Masingue et al., 2017; Piscosquito et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple clinical reports.

claim: Some cases of MFN2-associated lipomatosis have been compound heterozygous for R707W and a second, functionally null mutation.
source: Most cases have been homozygous for the R707W mutation, with others compound heterozygous for R707W and a second, functionally null mutation (Rocha et al., 2017; Sawyer et al., 2015; Capel et al., 2018; Carr et al., 2015; Masingue et al., 2017; Piscosquito et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical reports.

claim: Arginine 707 lies in the highly conserved heptad-repeat (HR)2 region of MFN2.
source: Arginine 707 lies in the highly conserved heptad-repeat (HR)2 region of MFN2 but consensus on the precise orientation and/or function of this domain has not yet been established (Mattie et al., 2018).
evidence: This is structural information about the protein, supported by a citation.

claim: Consensus on the precise orientation and/or function of the HR2 domain has not yet been established.
source: Arginine 707 lies in the highly conserved heptad-repeat (HR)2 region of MFN2 but consensus on the precise orientation and/or function of this domain has not yet been established (Mattie et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, supported by a citation.

claim: The HR2 domains of MFN1 and/or MFN2 face the cytosol and interact in trans, forming mitofusin homodimers or heterodimers required for mitochondrial fusion and tethering.
source: The dominant model holds that the HR2 domains of Mitofusin 1 (MFN1) and/or MFN2 face the cytosol and interact in trans, forming mitofusin homodimers or heterodimers required for mitochondrial fusion and tethering to other organelles (Koshiba et al., 2004; Franco et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a description of the dominant model in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The R707W mutation may disrupt mitofusin binding and subsequent oligomerisation and mitochondrial fusion/tethering.
source: The R707W mutation may disrupt this binding and subsequent MFN oligomerisation and mitochondrial fusion/tethering.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the location of the mutation.

claim: Global knock-out of Mfn1, Mfn2, Opa1, and Drp1 in mice confers embryonic lethality.
source: Global knock-out of the core mitochondrial fusion-fission machinery proteins Mfn1, Mfn2, Opa1, and Drp1 in mice confers embryonic lethality in all cases (Davies et al., 2007; Ishihara et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior mouse genetic studies.

claim: Homozygous Mfn2 H361Y knock-in mice were embryonically lethal due to complete loss of detectable Mfn2 protein.
source: H361Y was also embryonically lethal due to complete loss of detectable Mfn2 protein (Misko et al., 2010), while homozygous R94W mice died at post-natal day 1 (Strickland et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior mouse study.

claim: Homozygous Mfn2 R94W mice died at post-natal day 1.
source: H361Y was also embryonically lethal due to complete loss of detectable Mfn2 protein (Misko et al., 2010), while homozygous R94W mice died at post-natal day 1 (Strickland et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior mouse study.

claim: Mfn2R94W is expressed but is GTPase defective, increasing mitochondrial fragmentation and preventing formation of Mfn2 homodimers.
source: Mfn2R94W is expressed but is GTPase defective, increasing mitochondrial fragmentation and preventing formation of Mfn2 homodimers (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Adipose-specific Adipoq::Cre Mfn2 knock-out increased fat mass, attributed to reduced energy expenditure.
source: Adipose-specific Adipoq::Cre Mfn2 knock-out increased fat mass, attributed to reduced energy expenditure, whether it occurred in embryonic life (Boutant et al., 2017) or was induced by tamoxifen in adult mice (Mancini et al., 2019), with ultrastructural evidence of more rounded mitochondria with fewer lipid droplet contacts (Boutant et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior mouse studies.

claim: Adipoq::Cre driven and Ucp1::Cre driven Mfn2 knock-out caused cold intolerance with 'whitened' brown adipose tissue.
source: Both Adipoq::Cre driven (adipose-specific) and Ucp1::Cre driven (brown adipose-specific) Mfn2 knock-out also caused cold intolerance with 'whitened' brown adipose tissue (Mahdaviani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior mouse study.

claim: Leptin concentration was higher and adiponectin concentration lower in the tamoxifen-inducible adult Adipoq::Cre Mfn2 knockout model.
source: Plasma leptin concentrations were not reported in Adipoq-Cre or Ucp1::Cre Mfn2 knock-outs, but leptin concentration was higher and adiponectin concentration lower in the tamoxifen-inducible adult Adipoq::Cre Mfn2 knockout model (Mancini et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior mouse study.

claim: Mfn2R707W/R707W mice were generated by CRISPR-Cas9 genomic engineering using an ssODN template recoding Arginine to Tryptophan in codon 707.
source: Mfn2R707W/R707W mice were generated by CRISPR-Cas9 genomic engineering using an ssODN (single-stranded oligo donor) template recoding Arginine to Tryptophan in codon 707 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the method used to generate the mice, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: A single round of targeting yielded one founder (F0) mouse.
source: A single round of targeting yielded one founder (F0) mouse (Figure 1B) which was used to expand a colony on a C57/BL6J background.
evidence: This is a statement about the efficiency of the CRISPR targeting, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: An additional silent mutation introducing an EcoRV restriction site was introduced to facilitate genotyping.
source: An additional silent mutation introducing an EcoRV restriction site was introduced to facilitate genotyping (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This describes a technical aspect of the mouse generation, with reference to Figure 1C and D.

claim: No consistent differences in Mfn1 or Mfn2 expression were observed in inguinal WAT, liver, heart, or skeletal muscle in both chow and HFD fed Mfn2R707W/R707W mice relative to WT.
source: We observed no consistent differences in Mfn1 or Mfn2 expression, relative to WT, in inguinal white adipose tissue (WAT), liver, heart, or skeletal muscle in both chow and high-fat diet (HFD) fed mice (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–4).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis shown in the figures.

claim: In BAT, expression of Mfn1 was lower in KI than in WT mice fed with chow diet for 6 months.
source: However, in brown adipose tissue (BAT) expression of Mfn1 was lower in KI than in WT mice fed with chow diet for 6 months (Figure 1—figure supplements 1D and 2D).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis shown in the figure supplements.

claim: Expression of Mfn1 was lower in KI than WT mice after only 4 weeks of chow diet in BAT.
source: Similarly, expression of Mfn1 was lower in KI than WT mice after only 4 weeks of chow diet (Figure 1—figure supplements 1G and 2G).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis shown in the figure supplements.

claim: In HFD-fed mice, both Mfn1 and Mfn2 expression was lower in BAT in KI compared to WT mice.
source: In HFD-fed mice, both Mfn1 and Mfn2 expression was lower in BAT in KI compared to WT mice (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplements 3D and 4D).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis shown in the figures.

claim: In epididymal WAT, expression of Mfn1 was lower in KI than in WT mice fed with chow diet.
source: In epididymal WAT, expression of Mfn1 was also lower in KI than in WT mice fed with chow diet (Figure 1—figure supplements 1F and 2F), but no differences were observed in HFD-fed mice (Figure 1—figure supplements 3F and 4F).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis shown in the figure supplements.

claim: The R707W missense mutation does not directly reduce expression of Mfn2.
source: We interpret these data as suggesting that the R707W missense mutation does not directly reduce expression of Mfn2, nor does it result in a compensatory change in Mfn1 in most tissues.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the western blot data.

claim: The R707W mutation does not result in a compensatory change in Mfn1 in most tissues.
source: We interpret these data as suggesting that the R707W missense mutation does not directly reduce expression of Mfn2, nor does it result in a compensatory change in Mfn1 in most tissues.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the western blot data.

claim: In BAT, the cellular perturbation induced in brown adipocytes is associated with a modest reduction in expression of Mfn1 and 2.
source: However, in BAT the data suggests that the cellular perturbation induced in brown adipocytes is associated with a very modest reduction in expression of Mfn1 and 2.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the western blot data from BAT.

claim: In Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, mitochondria from BAT had a tendency to exhibit a decreased mitochondrial perimeter compared to WT mice.
source: In BAT, mitochondria from KI mice had a tendency to exhibit a decreased mitochondrial perimeter compared to WT mice (Figure 2B), but significantly reduced size, assessed by the mitochondrial cross-sectional length/ width aspect ratio analysis (Figure 2C), indicating that Mfn2R707W leads to mitochondrial fragmentation in BAT.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mitochondria in BAT from Mfn2R707W/R707W mice had significantly reduced size, assessed by aspect ratio analysis, indicating mitochondrial fragmentation.
source: In BAT, mitochondria from KI mice had a tendency to exhibit a decreased mitochondrial perimeter compared to WT mice (Figure 2B), but significantly reduced size, assessed by the mitochondrial cross-sectional length/ width aspect ratio analysis (Figure 2C), indicating that Mfn2R707W leads to mitochondrial fragmentation in BAT.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Mfn2R707W leads to mitochondrial fragmentation in BAT.
source: In BAT, mitochondria from KI mice had a tendency to exhibit a decreased mitochondrial perimeter compared to WT mice (Figure 2B), but significantly reduced size, assessed by the mitochondrial cross-sectional length/ width aspect ratio analysis (Figure 2C), indicating that Mfn2R707W leads to mitochondrial fragmentation in BAT.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the TEM data.

claim: Double membrane-bound structures representing autophagosomes consistent with mitophagy were observed in lipomatous adipose tissue from human patients with the MFN2R707W mutation.
source: Double membrane-bound structures representing autophagosomes consistent with mitophagy were observed in lipomatous adipose tissue from human patients with the MFN2R707W mutation (Rocha et al., 2017), but these were not identified in the murine tissues examined.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior human tissue analysis.

claim: Autophagosomes consistent with mitophagy were not identified in the murine tissues examined.
source: Double membrane-bound structures representing autophagosomes consistent with mitophagy were observed in lipomatous adipose tissue from human patients with the MFN2R707W mutation (Rocha et al., 2017), but these were not identified in the murine tissues examined.
evidence: This is based on examination of TEM images from the mice.

claim: The extent of mitochondrial-lipid droplet contacts was reduced in BAT from Mfn2R707W/R707W animals.
source: Mitofusins may mediate contact between mitochondria and lipid droplets (Boutant et al., 2017), and the extent of these contacts was reduced in BAT from KI animals (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Mitochondrial cristae were disrupted in BAT from Mfn2R707W/R707W animals compared to WT.
source: In addition, mitochondrial cristae were disrupted in KI compared to WT animals (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Similar mitochondrial fragmentation and cristae defects were observed in inguinal and epididymal WAT.
source: In both inguinal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C) and epididymal WAT (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–F), similar mitochondrial fragmentation and cristae defects were observed.
evidence: This is based on TEM analysis shown in the figure supplements.

claim: No change in mitochondrial morphology, cristae number, or cristae structure was seen in the heart, skeletal muscle, or liver of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: In contrast, no change in mitochondrial morphology, cristae number, or cristae structure was seen in the heart, skeletal muscle, or liver of KI mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on TEM analysis shown in the figure supplement.

claim: In Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, mtDNA was reduced in BAT in both diet conditions.
source: In Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, mtDNA was reduced in BAT in both diet conditions, but not in any other tissue analysed (WAT, heart, skeletal muscle, or liver) (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is based on qPCR measurements of mtDNA shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: mtDNA was not reduced in WAT, heart, skeletal muscle, or liver of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: In Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, mtDNA was reduced in BAT in both diet conditions, but not in any other tissue analysed (WAT, heart, skeletal muscle, or liver) (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is based on qPCR measurements shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: Immunoblotting of electron transport chain components from chow fed animals showed no changes in liver or heart.
source: Immunoblotting of electron transport chain components from chow fed animals showed no changes in liver or heart (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A–B).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis shown in the figure supplements.

claim: mtCo1 (complex IV) and Ndufb8 (complex I) were reduced in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice in brown and white adipose tissue.
source: However, mtCo1 (complex IV) and Ndufb8 (complex I) were reduced in KI mice in brown and white adipose tissue (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C–E and Figure 2—figure supplement 4C–E).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis shown in the figure supplements.

claim: Uqcrc2 (complex III) was lower in inguinal WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: In addition, Uqcrc2 (complex III) was also lower in inguinal WAT.
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis.

claim: No significant differences in oxidative capacity were detected between WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W mitochondria isolated from BAT and liver by high-resolution respirometry.
source: To determine if these changes altered mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, we assessed oxidative capacity in freshly isolated mitochondria from BAT and liver by high-resolution respirometry using Oroboros Oxygraphy. No significant differences were detected between WT and KI mitochondria (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A–B).
evidence: This is based on Oroboros respirometry measurements shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Despite a trend towards reduced thermogenic capacity in Mfn2R707W/R707W animals, the difference was not significant.
source: We further assessed mitochondrial function in BAT in vivo by challenging mice with noradrenaline in cold (10 degrees) or thermoneutral (30 degrees) conditions to determine maximum thermogenic capacity. Again, despite a trend towards reduced thermogenic capacity in KI animals, the difference was not significant, and both groups manifested the expected increase in energy expenditure at 10 °C (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C–G).
evidence: This is based on calorimetry measurements shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Both WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W groups manifested the expected increase in energy expenditure at 10 °C.
source: We further assessed mitochondrial function in BAT in vivo by challenging mice with noradrenaline in cold (10 degrees) or thermoneutral (30 degrees) conditions to determine maximum thermogenic capacity. Again, despite a trend towards reduced thermogenic capacity in KI animals, the difference was not significant, and both groups manifested the expected increase in energy expenditure at 10 °C (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C–G).
evidence: This is based on calorimetry measurements shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Whole body mass and composition were similar in Mfn2R707W/R707W and WT mice throughout the study period.
source: Whole body mass and composition, and masses of individual adipose depots and other organs were similar in KI and WT mice throughout the study period (Table 1, Figure 3A–C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is based on body weight measurements and TD-NMR data shown in the table and figures.

claim: Masses of individual adipose depots and other organs were similar in Mfn2R707W/R707W and WT mice throughout the study period.
source: Whole body mass and composition, and masses of individual adipose depots and other organs were similar in KI and WT mice throughout the study period (Table 1, Figure 3A–C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is based on tissue weight measurements shown in the table and figures.

claim: No difference in hepatic steatosis was detected histologically in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Moreover, no difference in hepatic steatosis nor lipid droplet size was detected histologically in BAT or WAT (Figure 3D–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F–G).
evidence: This is based on histological analysis shown in the figures.

claim: No difference in lipid droplet size was detected histologically in BAT or WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Moreover, no difference in hepatic steatosis nor lipid droplet size was detected histologically in BAT or WAT (Figure 3D–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F–G).
evidence: This is based on histological analysis shown in the figures.

claim: Fasting serum glucose, insulin, triglycerides, cholesterol, lactate, and liver transaminase concentrations showed no difference between WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: In keeping with the normal body composition, fasting serum glucose, insulin, triglycerides, cholesterol, lactate, and liver transaminase concentrations showed no difference between WT and KI mice (Figure 3F–I and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, H).
evidence: This is based on serum biochemistry measurements shown in the figures.

claim: Dynamic testing of glucose and insulin tolerance was similar between WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W genotypes.
source: There was also no differences in hepatic expression of genes related to lipid metabolism or steatohepatitis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). Dynamic testing of glucose and insulin tolerance was also similar between genotypes (Figure 3G–K).
evidence: This is based on IPGTT and IPITT data shown in the figures.

claim: There was no difference in body weight between high-fat fed WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W female mice.
source: Similar results were observed in female mice harboring the Mfn2R707W mutation. Specifically, there was no difference in body weight, fat mass, fasting glucose or insulin between high-fat fed WT and KI mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is based on measurements in female mice shown in the figure supplement.

claim: There was no difference in fat mass between high-fat fed WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W female mice.
source: Similar results were observed in female mice harboring the Mfn2R707W mutation. Specifically, there was no difference in body weight, fat mass, fasting glucose or insulin between high-fat fed WT and KI mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is based on measurements in female mice shown in the figure supplement.

claim: There was no difference in fasting glucose between high-fat fed WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W female mice.
source: Similar results were observed in female mice harboring the Mfn2R707W mutation. Specifically, there was no difference in body weight, fat mass, fasting glucose or insulin between high-fat fed WT and KI mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is based on measurements in female mice shown in the figure supplement.

claim: There was no difference in fasting insulin between high-fat fed WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W female mice.
source: Similar results were observed in female mice harboring the Mfn2R707W mutation. Specifically, there was no difference in body weight, fat mass, fasting glucose or insulin between high-fat fed WT and KI mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is based on measurements in female mice shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Atf4 plays a crucial role in the transcriptional response to mitochondrial dysfunction.
source: Although details of the integration of these mechanisms in different tissue and cellular contexts are not fully elucidated, it is clear that the transcription factor Atf4 plays a crucial role (Lu et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Atf4 is translationally upregulated following phosphorylation of eIF2α.
source: Atf4 is translationally upregulated following phosphorylation of eIF2α, which is a point of convergence of several cellular stress sensing pathways.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the ISR mechanism.

claim: The canonical eIF2α kinase HRI is most closely implicated in linking mitochondrial dysfunction to eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: The canonical eIF2α kinase HRI is most closely implicated in linking mitochondrial dysfunction to eIF2α phosphorylation (Guo et al., 2020; Fessler et al., 2020), but mTORC1 appears to play a role in Atf4 upregulation independently of eIF2α phosphorylation (Ben-Sahra et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: mTORC1 appears to play a role in Atf4 upregulation independently of eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: The canonical eIF2α kinase HRI is most closely implicated in linking mitochondrial dysfunction to eIF2α phosphorylation (Guo et al., 2020; Fessler et al., 2020), but mTORC1 appears to play a role in Atf4 upregulation independently of eIF2α phosphorylation (Ben-Sahra et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Strong transcriptional evidence of ISR activation was found in adipose tissue of patients with MFN2R707W-related lipodystrophy.
source: Strong transcriptional evidence of ISR activation was found in adipose tissue of patients with MFN2R707W-related lipodystrophy (Rocha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: mRNA levels of Atf4, Atf5, and Ddit3 (Chop) were increased in BAT and epididymal WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: mRNA levels of Atf4, Atf5, and Ddit3 (Chop), all sentinel markers of the ISR, were increased in BAT and epididymal WAT of KI mice (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Ddit3 was higher in inguinal WAT from Mfn2R707W/R707W animals.
source: Ddit3 was also higher in inguinal WAT from KI animals.
evidence: This is based on qPCR data.

claim: mRNA levels of Atf4, Atf5, and Ddit3 (Chop) were unchanged in liver, heart, and skeletal muscle of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, except for a 1.4-fold rise in Atf5 in skeletal muscle only.
source: mRNA levels of Atf4, Atf5, and Ddit3 (Chop) were unchanged in liver, heart, and skeletal muscle, except for a 1.4-fold rise in Atf5 (p.adj=0.03) in skeletal muscle only.
evidence: This is based on qPCR data.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α was strongly increased in BAT and WAT in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Phosphorylation of eIF2α and protein expression of Mthfd2, an Atf4-upregulated enzyme playing a rate-limiting role in mitochondrial one carbon metabolism (Shin et al., 2017; Forsström et al., 2019; Khan et al., 2017), were also both strongly increased in BAT and in WAT in KI mice (Figure 4D–F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E–G and Figure 4—figure supplement 2), whereas they were unchanged in the liver, skeletal muscle, and heart.
evidence: This is based on western blot data shown in the figures.

claim: Protein expression of Mthfd2 was strongly increased in BAT and WAT in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Phosphorylation of eIF2α and protein expression of Mthfd2, an Atf4-upregulated enzyme playing a rate-limiting role in mitochondrial one carbon metabolism (Shin et al., 2017; Forsström et al., 2019; Khan et al., 2017), were also both strongly increased in BAT and in WAT in KI mice (Figure 4D–F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E–G and Figure 4—figure supplement 2), whereas they were unchanged in the liver, skeletal muscle, and heart.
evidence: This is based on western blot data shown in the figures.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α and protein expression of Mthfd2 were unchanged in the liver, skeletal muscle, and heart of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Phosphorylation of eIF2α and protein expression of Mthfd2, an Atf4-upregulated enzyme playing a rate-limiting role in mitochondrial one carbon metabolism (Shin et al., 2017; Forsström et al., 2019; Khan et al., 2017), were also both strongly increased in BAT and in WAT in KI mice (Figure 4D–F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E–G and Figure 4—figure supplement 2), whereas they were unchanged in the liver, skeletal muscle, and heart.
evidence: This is based on western blot data shown in the figures.

claim: mRNA expression of Gdf15 and Fgf21 trended towards an increase in adipose tissue of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, but serum concentrations were unchanged.
source: mRNA expression of two important secreted mediators of the organismal metabolic response to mitochondrial dysfunction, Gdf15 and Fgf21, trended towards an increase in adipose tissue, but serum concentrations were unchanged in KI mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is based on qPCR and serum measurements shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The unchanged serum GDF15 and FGF21 in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice differs from observations in patients with MFN2R707W-related lipodystrophy.
source: This differs from observations in patients with MFN2R707W-related lipodystrophy (Khan et al., 2017; Fisher and Maratos-Flier, 2016; Patel et al., 2019), and may relate to the fact that such patients manifest non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, which was not seen in the KI animals.
evidence: This is an interpretation comparing mouse and human data, supported by citations.

claim: Induction of the ISR was confirmed in both BAT and WAT by bulk RNA sequencing.
source: To obtain an unbiased view of the transcriptional consequences of the lipodystrophy-associated Mfn2 mutation, we next applied bulk RNA sequencing (RNAseq) to BAT and inguinal WAT from HFD-fed mice. Inguinal, rather than epididymal, WAT was selected as subcutaneous adipose tissue is predominantly affected in human MFN2-related and other partial lipodystrophies (Mann and Savage, 2019). Induction of the ISR was confirmed in both BAT and WAT (Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 5), with the "unfolded protein response" gene set, a surrogate for the ISR, the top upregulated gene set in BAT and 6th in inguinal WAT.
evidence: This is based on RNAseq data and pathway analysis shown in the figures.

claim: The 'unfolded protein response' gene set was the top upregulated gene set in BAT and 6th in inguinal WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Induction of the ISR was confirmed in both BAT and WAT (Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 5), with the "unfolded protein response" gene set, a surrogate for the ISR, the top upregulated gene set in BAT and 6th in inguinal WAT.
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis of RNAseq data shown in the figures.

claim: Atf5 and Mthfd2 were among the most highly upregulated mRNAs in both BAT and WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Atf5 and Mthfd2 were confirmed among the most highly upregulated mRNAs in both tissues, and a range of other well established ISR genes also showed increased expression.
evidence: This is based on RNAseq data.

claim: The top upregulated gene set in inguinal WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice was 'oxidative phosphorylation', driven solely by increased expression of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes.
source: The top upregulated gene set in inguinal WAT was 'oxidative phosphorylation', driven solely by increased expression of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis of RNAseq data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Mitochondria-encoded genes were nearly universally downregulated in inguinal WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: In contrast, mitochondria-encoded genes were nearly universally downregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I), recapitulating the pattern seen in affected human WAT (Rocha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The pattern of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes being upregulated while mitochondria-encoded genes are downregulated recapitulates the pattern seen in affected human WAT.
source: In contrast, mitochondria-encoded genes were nearly universally downregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I), recapitulating the pattern seen in affected human WAT (Rocha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior human data, supported by a citation.

claim: The 'mTorc signalling' gene set was the second most upregulated group in BAT and third most upregulated in WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Another finding common to mouse and human was the transcriptional evidence of mTORC1 activation. The 'mTorc signalling' gene set was the second most upregulated group in BAT and third most upregulated in WAT (Figure 4—figure supplement 5B, E).
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis of RNAseq data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: mTORC1 activation is consistent with the proposed role for mTORC1 in mediating the proximal ISR.
source: This activation is consistent with the proposed role for mTORC1 in mediating the proximal ISR (Ben-Sahra et al., 2016), and is of interest given accumulating evidence that the mTORC1 inhibitor sirolimus may exert beneficial effects in various mitochondrial diseases (Johnson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in the context of prior research, supported by citations.

claim: The 'adipogenesis' gene set was upregulated in inguinal WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice under both diet conditions.
source: Although no increase in adipose tissue mass was seen in Mfn2R707W mice the 'adipogenesis' gene set was upregulated in inguinal WAT under both diet conditions (Figure 4H, Figure 4—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis of RNAseq data shown in the figures.

claim: The most consistent finding in the adipogenesis gene set was downregulation of Adipoq and Lep in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: However, closer inspection revealed a mixed profile of individual gene expression. The most consistent finding was downregulation of the adipokine-encoding mature adipocyte genes Adipoq and Lep in Mfn2R707W mice (discussed below).
evidence: This is based on examination of individual gene expression in the RNAseq data.

claim: Adipoq and Lep were also downregulated in BAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: Adipoq and Lep were also downregulated in BAT (fold changes 0.64 (p.adj=6.3 × 10–4) and 0.31 (p.adj=0.03) respectively), but the adipogenesis gene set was not enriched overall (Figure 4—figure supplement 5E).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The signature of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) was the most strongly down-regulated set in mouse BAT and WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: To assess for other potential drivers of adipose hyperplasia, we also examined downregulated gene sets. The signature of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) was the most strongly down-regulated set in mouse BAT and WAT (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 5C, F), and was also previously found to be downregulated in overgrown human WAT in MFN2-associated multiple symmetric lipomatosis (Rocha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis of RNAseq data shown in the figures.

claim: The EMT signature was also previously found to be downregulated in overgrown human WAT in MFN2-associated multiple symmetric lipomatosis.
source: The signature of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) was the most strongly down-regulated set in mouse BAT and WAT (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 5C, F), and was also previously found to be downregulated in overgrown human WAT in MFN2-associated multiple symmetric lipomatosis (Rocha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior human transcriptomic data.

claim: Comparison of inguinal WAT from HFD-fed and chow-fed Mfn2R707W/R707W mice revealed strikingly concordant findings.
source: We next sought to assess whether the increased demand for adipose expansion imposed by HFD feeding exacerbates the transcriptional consequences of Mfn2 R707W homozygosity. RNAseq was thus undertaken of inguinal WAT from mice maintained on HFD for 6 months. Comparison to WT animals revealed strikingly concordant findings to those seen in chow-fed mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 5G).
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNAseq data from different diet conditions shown in the figure supplement.

claim: No general differences were seen in the magnitude of transcriptional changes induced by Mfn2 R707W homozygosity between chow and HFD conditions.
source: No general differences were seen in the magnitude of transcriptional changes induced by Mfn2 R707W homozygosity between conditions.
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNAseq data from different diet conditions.

claim: The group of mRNAs related to cholesterol homeostasis was the top downregulated gene set in inguinal WAT in HFD-fed Mfn2R707W/R707W animals but was not significantly altered on chow.
source: An exception was the group of mRNAs related to cholesterol homeostasis, for which diet strikingly modified the effect of genotype. They were the top downregulated gene set in inguinal WAT in HFD-fed animals but were not significantly altered on chow in the same depot and were upregulated in BAT (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 5E).
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis of RNAseq data shown in the figures.

claim: Lower expression of key enzymes in cholesterol metabolism in WAT on HFD is consistent with the response to inhibition of the mitochondrial respiratory chain in primary human fibroblasts.
source: Lower expression of key enzymes in cholesterol metabolism (e.g. Hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA synthase [Hmgcs1], mevalonate kinase [Mvk], and squalene monooxygenase [Sqle]) in WAT on HFD is consistent with the response to inhibition of the mitochondrial respiratory chain in primary human fibroblasts (Wall et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior research findings, supported by a citation.

claim: Mfn2R707W/R707W mice showed low-serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations on both chow and HFD.
source: Mirroring these human observations, KI mice showed low-serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations on both chow and HFD (Figure 5A–C), although unlike humans, the mice had normal fat mass and insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is based on serum measurements shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: Unlike humans with MFN2 R707W mutations, Mfn2R707W/R707W mice had normal fat mass and insulin sensitivity.
source: Mirroring these human observations, KI mice showed low-serum leptin and adiponectin concentrations on both chow and HFD (Figure 5A–C), although unlike humans, the mice had normal fat mass and insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is a comparison of mouse and human phenotypes based on the data presented.

claim: In both WT and Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, serum leptin concentrations correlated positively with whole body adiposity on chow and HFD.
source: In both WT and KI mice, serum leptin concentrations correlated positively with whole body adiposity on chow and HFD, but a generalised linear model revealed marked attenuation of the relationship between serum leptin concentration and adipose mass in the KI mice (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis shown in the figures.

claim: A generalised linear model revealed marked attenuation of the relationship between serum leptin concentration and adipose mass in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: In both WT and KI mice, serum leptin concentrations correlated positively with whole body adiposity on chow and HFD, but a generalised linear model revealed marked attenuation of the relationship between serum leptin concentration and adipose mass in the KI mice (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on statistical modeling of the data shown in the figures.

claim: Immunoblotting of WAT samples from HFD-fed Mfn2R707W/R707W mice confirmed that both leptin and adiponectin expression was reduced.
source: Immunoblotting of WAT samples from KI mice fed a HFD confirmed that both leptin and adiponectin expression was reduced (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on western blot data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: In female Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, serum adiponectin was significantly lower.
source: Findings were similar in female mice, in which serum adiponectin was significantly lower in KI mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F), with a trend towards lower leptin (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G–I).
evidence: This is based on serum measurements in female mice shown in the figure supplement.

claim: In female Mfn2R707W/R707W mice, there was a trend towards lower leptin.
source: Findings were similar in female mice, in which serum adiponectin was significantly lower in KI mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F), with a trend towards lower leptin (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G–I).
evidence: This is based on serum measurements in female mice shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Lep mRNA in inguinal WAT was lower in Mfn2R707W/R707W than in WT mice under both chow and HFD conditions.
source: RNAseq showed Lep mRNA in inguinal WAT to be lower in Mfn2R707W than in WT mice under both chow (fold change 0.35; p.adj=3.2 × 10–4, Figure 4—figure supplement 5A) and HFD (fold change 0.66; p.adj=5.3 × 10–4, Figure 4G).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq data shown in the figures.

claim: Adipoq mRNA was significantly lower in inguinal WAT of Mfn2R707W/R707W mice in both chow and HF-fed conditions.
source: Adipoq mRNA was also significantly lower in chow (fold change 0.66; p.adj=2.7 × 10–4, Figure 4—figure supplement 5A) and HF-fed mice (fold change 0.57; p.adj=3.3 × 10–15, Figure 4G).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq data shown in the figures.

claim: RT-qPCR analysis confirmed lower Lep mRNA in epididymal WAT from chow fed Mfn2R707W/R707W animals.
source: RT-qPCR analysis confirmed lower Lep mRNA in epididymal WAT from chow fed Mfn2R707W animals (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: RT-qPCR analysis found 50% lower Adipoq mRNA in both inguinal and epididymal WAT in chow fed Mfn2R707W/R707W mice and in inguinal WAT from HFD fed Mfn2R707W/R707W mice.
source: RT-qPCR analysis also found 50% lower Adipoq mRNA in both inguinal and epididymal WAT in chow fed Mfn2R707W mice and in inguinal WAT from HFD fed Mfn2R707W mice (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Explants from Mfn2R707W/R707W mice fed on HFD for 4 weeks showed lower secretion of leptin and adiponectin per gram of tissue.
source: To assess leptin secretion directly, we studied production of adipokines from adipose explants. Explants from KI mice fed on HFD for 4 weeks showed lower secretion of leptin and adiponectin per gram of tissue (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is based on ex vivo explant secretion experiments shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Mfn2R707W/R707W explants exhibited minimal increase in leptin secretion after insulin and dexamethasone stimulation.
source: KI explants also exhibited minimal increase in leptin secretion after insulin and dexamethasone stimulation.
evidence: This is based on ex vivo explant secretion experiments.

claim: Adipoq mRNA was lower in Mfn2R707W/R707W explants at baseline.
source: Adipoq mRNA was lower in KI than WT explants at baseline whereas Lep mRNA was no different at baseline but failed to increase in KI explants following insulin and dexamethasone stimulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on qPCR analysis of explants shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Lep mRNA was no different at baseline in Mfn2R707W/R707W explants but failed to increase following insulin and dexamethasone stimulation.
source: Adipoq mRNA was lower in KI than WT explants at baseline whereas Lep mRNA was no different at baseline but failed to increase in KI explants following insulin and dexamethasone stimulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on qPCR analysis of explants shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Thapsigargin and tunicamycin induced the ISR in primary mouse adipocytes, confirmed by increased Atf4 and Ddit3 mRNA and/or protein expression, and by eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: To assess whether induction of the ISR in adipose tissue may be responsible for the relative leptin deficiency in both humans and mice homozygous for MFN2 R707W, we studied adipocytes freshly isolated from mouse gonadal fat in floating culture, adapting a recently described protocol (Li et al., 2021). We induced the ISR using each of two different well characterised activators, namely thapsigargin (TG), an inhibitor of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) Ca2+ ATPase that depletes ER calcium (Wictome et al., 1992; Harding et al., 2000), or tunicamycin (TN), which blocks protein glycosylation. ISR induction was confirmed by increased Atf4 and Ddit3 mRNA and/or protein expression, and by eIF2α phosphorylation (Figure 5F–L).
evidence: This is based on experiments in primary adipocytes shown in Figure 5F-L.

claim: Lep mRNA was modestly reduced by thapsigargin but not by tunicamycin in primary adipocytes.
source: Lep mRNA was modestly reduced by TG but not by TN (Figure 5H), whereas both agents reduced intracellular leptin protein expression (Figure 5L) and secretion (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is based on qPCR and western blot data from primary adipocytes shown in the figures.

claim: Both thapsigargin and tunicamycin reduced intracellular leptin protein expression in primary adipocytes.
source: Lep mRNA was modestly reduced by TG but not by TN (Figure 5H), whereas both agents reduced intracellular leptin protein expression (Figure 5L) and secretion (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is based on western blot data from primary adipocytes shown in the figures.

claim: Both thapsigargin and tunicamycin reduced leptin secretion from primary adipocytes.
source: Lep mRNA was modestly reduced by TG but not by TN (Figure 5H), whereas both agents reduced intracellular leptin protein expression (Figure 5L) and secretion (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is based on secretion assays from primary adipocytes shown in the figures.

claim: Expression of adiponectin was reduced by thapsigargin and tunicamycin without a change in mRNA level in primary adipocytes.
source: Expression of adiponectin was also reduced without a change in mRNA level whereas expression of Akt and the insulin receptor beta subunit were not altered (Figure 5I and K & L).
evidence: This is based on qPCR and western blot data from primary adipocytes shown in the figures.

claim: Expression of Akt and the insulin receptor beta subunit were not altered by ISR induction in primary adipocytes.
source: Expression of adiponectin was also reduced without a change in mRNA level whereas expression of Akt and the insulin receptor beta subunit were not altered (Figure 5I and K & L).
evidence: This is based on western blot data from primary adipocytes shown in the figures.

claim: Serum adipsin concentrations were significantly lower in Mfn2R707W/R707W mice than in WT controls in both chow- and HFD-fed mice.
source: In seeking to validate this notion, we proceeded to measure the serum concentration of adipsin, another 'adipokine' selectively secreted by adipocytes. Serum adipsin concentrations were significantly lower in the KI mice than in WT controls in both chow- and HFD-fed mice (Figure 5M), suggesting that low serum leptin and adiponectin may be part of a wider pattern of reduced adipocyte-derived secreted proteins in MFN2R707W KI mice.
evidence: This is based on serum adipsin measurements shown in Figure 5M.

claim: Low serum leptin and adiponectin may be part of a wider pattern of reduced adipocyte-derived secreted proteins in MFN2R707W KI mice.
source: Serum adipsin concentrations were significantly lower in the KI mice than in WT controls in both chow- and HFD-fed mice (Figure 5M), suggesting that low serum leptin and adiponectin may be part of a wider pattern of reduced adipocyte-derived secreted proteins in MFN2R707W KI mice.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the adipsin data.

claim: Homozygous Mfn2R707W/R707W mice were viable and bred normally.
source: Homozygous Mfn2 R707W mice, in contrast, were viable and bred normally, showing that Mfn2 R707W retains significant function.
evidence: This is based on observation of the mouse colony.

claim: Mfn2 R707W retains significant function.
source: Homozygous Mfn2 R707W mice, in contrast, were viable and bred normally, showing that Mfn2 R707W retains significant function.
evidence: This is an inference from the viability and fertility of the mice.

claim: Mice lacking Mfn2 in all adipocytes did not show reduced adipose tissue but exhibited lower energy expenditure, reduced expression of multiple oxidative phosphorylation subunits, and impaired cold tolerance.
source: Mfn2 also has key metabolic functions in mature adipocytes: mice lacking Mfn2 in all adipocytes (Boutant et al., 2017) or in brown adipocytes alone (Mahdaviani et al., 2017) did not show reduced adipose tissue, but they did exhibit lower energy expenditure, reduced expression of multiple oxidative phosphorylation subunits, and impaired cold tolerance.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior mouse studies.

claim: Mice lacking Mfn2 in all adipocytes or in brown adipocytes alone were protected from systemic insulin resistance.
source: Paradoxically, however, both lines were protected from systemic insulin resistance.
evidence: This is based on prior mouse studies.

claim: Mice in which Mfn2 was deleted in all adipocytes in adulthood showed increased obesity and elevated blood glucose.
source: Mice in which Mfn2 was deleted in all adipocytes in adulthood showed increased obesity and elevated blood glucose (Mancini et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior mouse study.

claim: Homozygous Mfn2 R707W mice showed no overt change in adipose mass, metabolic function, or thermogenic capacity even though the genetic alteration was constitutional.
source: In contrast, homozygous Mfn2 R707W mice showed no overt change in adipose mass, metabolic function, or thermogenic capacity even though the genetic alteration was constitutional.
evidence: This is based on the phenotypic characterization data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The lack of overt phenotypic changes in homozygous Mfn2 R707W mice confirms some retained Mfn2 function also in adipose lineages.
source: This confirms some retained Mfn2 function also in adipose lineages.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison to complete Mfn2 knockout models.

claim: Primary anatomical and/or functional defects in humans with MFN2 R707W homozygosity have been observed only in adipose tissue and peripheral nerves.
source: Primary anatomical and/or functional defects in humans with MFN2 R707W homozygosity have been observed only in adipose tissue and peripheral nerves, with some but not all people reported to have sensorimotor neuropathy.
evidence: This is based on review of prior clinical reports.

claim: Some but not all people with MFN2 R707W homozygosity have been reported to have sensorimotor neuropathy.
source: Primary anatomical and/or functional defects in humans with MFN2 R707W homozygosity have been observed only in adipose tissue and peripheral nerves, with some but not all people reported to have sensorimotor neuropathy.
evidence: This is based on review of prior clinical reports.

claim: Homozygous Mfn2 R707W KI mice had no overt anatomical adipose abnormality.
source: Although homozygous Mfn2 R707W KI mice had no overt anatomical adipose abnormality, and failed to show obvious neurological phenotypes, ultrastructural studies did reveal mitochondrial network disruption in adipose tissues, but not liver, skeletal muscle, or heart.

claim: Homozygous Mfn2 R707W KI mice failed to show obvious neurological phenotypes.
